subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of nutrient deficiency in plants?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Increased resistance to diseases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nutrient deficiency** in plants occurs when an **essential element** is not available in the required concentration, leading to morphological changes and physiological disorders.
 
• **Low yield**: When plants lack primary nutrients like **Nitrogen (N)**, **Phosphorus (P)**, or **Potassium (K)**, their metabolic efficiency drops. This results in reduced production of seeds, fruits, and overall **biomass**, leading to a significantly **low yield** for farmers. ***Hence, statement 1 is a consequence.***
 
• **Affected reproduction**: Nutrients like **Boron** and **Phosphorus** are critical for the reproductive phase. Deficiency can lead to **delayed flowering**, poor **pollen germination**, and **abscission** of flowers or fruits, directly hindering the plant's ability to reproduce. ***Hence, statement 2 is a consequence.***
 
• **Poor growth**: Essential elements are structural and functional components of **cells**. For instance, **Nitrogen** is a part of **proteins** and **Magnesium** is the central atom of **chlorophyll**. Their absence causes **stunted growth**, reduced leaf size, and weak stems. ***Hence, statement 3 is a consequence.***
 
• **Increased resistance to diseases**: This is **incorrect** because nutrient-deficient plants actually become **more susceptible** to infections. Deficiency weakens **cell walls** and slows down the production of **secondary metabolites** (like phytoalexins) that defend against **pathogens**, **fungi**, and **bacteria**. ***Hence, statement 4 is NOT a consequence and is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Essential Elements**: There are **17 essential elements** required for plant growth. These are divided into **Macronutrients** (needed in large amounts) and **Micronutrients** (needed in traces).
 
• **Common Deficiency Symptoms**:
 
 
• **Chlorosis**: The loss of **chlorophyll** leading to yellowing of leaves. It is caused by the deficiency of **N, K, Mg, S, Fe, Mn, Zn,** and **Mo**.
 
• **Necrosis**: This is the **death of tissues**, particularly leaf tissue, often caused by the lack of **Ca, Mg, Cu,** and **K**.
 
• **Inhibition of Cell Division**: Lack of **N, K, S,** and **Mo** can prevent cells from dividing properly, leading to stunted development.
 
• **Delay in Flowering**: Elements like **N, S,** and **Mo**, if low in concentration, can significantly delay the **flowering** process in plants.
 
 
 
• **Critical Concentration**: The concentration of an essential element below which plant growth is retarded is termed as **critical concentration**.
 
• **Mobility of Nutrients**: If a nutrient is **mobile** (like **Nitrogen** or **Magnesium**), deficiency symptoms appear first in **older tissues**. If the nutrient is **immobile** (like **Calcium** or **Sulphur**), symptoms appear first in **younger tissues**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nitrogen (N)**: Highly mobile; required for **meristematic tissues** and **metabolic** activities.
 
• **Phosphorus (P)**: Component of **cell membranes**, **nucleic acids**, and all **phosphorylation** reactions.
 
• **Potassium (K)**: Helps in maintaining **anion-cation balance** in cells and is involved in **stomata opening and closing**.
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)**: Activates enzymes of **respiration** and **photosynthesis** and maintains **ribosome structure**.
 
• **Toxicity**: While deficiency is harmful, an excess of **micronutrients** can cause **toxicity**. For example, **Manganese (Mn)** toxicity can induce deficiencies of **Iron, Magnesium, and Calcium**.
